title: Rupee climbs past 93/$ as investors seek shelter in Indian stocks, shorts unwind - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Rupee trims 2026 losses to 3.5% from nearly 8% in May | Photo Credit: istock.com

The Indian ‌rupee strengthened past the psychologically important 93-per-dollar mark on Friday for the first time ​since April, as Indian equities attracted investors fleeing AI-driven markets and oil ⁠prices dropped, accelerating a sharp reversal in the currency's fortunes.

The rupee has struggled for most of 2026, threatening to breach record low levels as recently as last month. It has since recovered sharply, cutting year-to-date ‌losses to about 3% compared to nearly 8% at its weakest point in May and closing the week at 92.67, following its strongest session since ‌October 12.

Friday's gains accompanied gains in Indian stocks in the face of a worsening global ‌rout ⁠in AI-linked stocks. Asian shares logged their worst week since 2020. India's benchmark Nifty ⁠50, on the other hand, notched a fourth straight weekly gain.

Foreigners have poured $12 billion into Indian shares so far in November, the largest-ever monthly inflow, compared with more than $60 billion of selling from September 2024 to October ​2026.

"More balanced global investor positioning and ‌moderation in the oil price could see a sharp reversal in investor flows, to the benefit of the Indian stock market," said Edward Evans, portfolio manager at Ashmore Group.

The surge in inflows has sharply increased the supply of dollars, boosting the rupee at a ‌time when measures taken by the Reserve Bank of India have curbed demand.

Earlier ​this year, policymakers rolled out steps to alleviate sustained pressure on the local currency, including clamping down on speculative trades, attracting capital inflows from overseas Indians ⁠and shifting crude oil import-related dollar demand out of the spot market.

As the rupee struggled near record low levels of 97 last month, RBI chief Sanjay Malhotra had hinted that monetary tightening ‌could also be used to support the unit.

A sustained recovery may help reverse capital outflow-induced weakness in the currency, which has eroded returns for foreign investors and could deter further investments, analysts say.

The rupee has also benefited from a rush to unwind bearish wagers on the currency this week, with the flows concentrated in offshore markets, bankers said.

The reversal, which four bankers said was led by overseas hedge funds, has been aggressive ‌enough to lift the rupee to a rare premium in the non-deliverable forward markets.

The sentiment shift is also ​apparent in the options market, with a key gauge showing that demand for options betting on rupee weakness has eased relative to those betting on ⁠its strength.

"Importantly, the RBI is choosing to let the INR appreciate and not draw a floor by ⁠buying reserves to elicit a behavioural or expectation shift among exporters and offshore participants," said Dhiraj Nim, an economist and FX Strategist at ANZ.

Persistently elevated demand for ‌forward dollars -- typically from importers -- has been a sore spot for the rupee throughout this year.

A reduction in speculative dollar demand from companies and an unwinding of offshore wagers ​are both helping the rupee, according to an FX salesperson at a foreign bank.
